topics.topic: Behavior when approval digest mismatches but an active standing grant covers the node
questions: If an approval exists but no longer matches `request_digest`, and an active standing grant covers the node, must the kernel send under the grant immediately, or must it request a new approval?
When an approved-but-mismatched approval exists and an active grant also exists, does the kernel send under the grant or create a new approval request first?

quotes:
A difference voids the approval, not a
    standing grant: where the owner's active grant covers the node, the send
    goes under the grant without asking (A10 rule 1; owner, 2026-10-03, raised
    by State 2 round 30).

none when a `requested` one for it already exists, even if the request has
   changed since: when that one is approved and the send's digest differs, rule 1
   applies and a new approval is requested
judgement.why: One passage says a digest mismatch with an active grant sends without asking, while the other says a new approval is requested.

topics.topic: Whether authority checks apply to `read` operations and what authority is required
questions: When a `read` operation is executed or resumed after `service_unreachable`, should authority checks be skipped entirely, or should missing approval/grant make it wait for owner approval?
Does the authority step apply to `read` operations at all, and if so what counts as "authority" for a `read` element?

quotes:
At run time each `state-transition`, `external-effect` and
`destructive` node stops for the owner's approval of the exact operation, target
and input, unless the owner granted that exact flow version a standing approval
for that node; `destructive` never takes a grant.

Reaching an operation element runs in this order: the pre-send checks of
   A09 rule 6 — a failure writes the element's next NodeExecution,
   `operation_failed`; then the authority of A10 rule 1, checked as it stands
   now — without it the element waits for approval, and after the approval this
   order starts again; then, for an operation other than `read`, one store call
   writes the EffectAttempt `in_flight`, naming the authority it uses — the
   approval, the grant, or for a `draft-write` send the flow activation
   (A10 rule 6);
judgement.why: One passage limits approval stops to specific effect classes, while another applies an authority/approval wait step to any operation element.

topics.topic: Handling unknown `contract_version_id`/`binding_id` references in compose_and_prove (early refusal vs keep-then-fail)
questions: If a composed flow version names an unknown contract_version_id or binding_id, is the request refused as `unknown reference` before keeping any version, or is the version kept and proof fails in phase 1?

topics.topic: Refusal precedence when compose request has both purpose-consistency and malformed-structure faults
questions: If a compose request both violates purpose consistency and has one of A05 rule 7 malformed-structure faults, which refusal must be returned first?

topics.topic: Required kernel state/recovery when outcome persistence fails after a service call completes
questions: If the service call completed but this post-send store call fails, what state must the kernel force (e.g., convert to unknown, stop process, retry write), given effect may have happened and no outcome record was written?

topics.topic: Validation stage for caller-supplied `effect_class`/`idempotency_key_fields` in binding proposals (schema-forbidden vs A08-forbidden)
questions: Should `effect_class`/`idempotency_key_fields` be schema-allowed-but-forbidden-by-A08 (manifest-mismatch style refusal), or schema-forbidden as unknown fields (A16 refusal before A08 checks)?

topics.topic: Whether malformed `idempotency_key` text is enforced or ignored for `read` operations
questions: For a `read` operation, must malformed `idempotency_key` text (duplicates, empty parts, invalid names) still refuse proposal/acceptance, or be ignored entirely?
